audit_findings.title: The acquisition-perimeter contract is internally inconsistent
audit_findings.magnitude: DD-Scientific consideration $53.6m; any Varex transaction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A wrong transaction identity or cutoff can omit acquisition consideration, financing, acquired OE or dilution from the bridge and forecast perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: In the first quarter of 2026, the Company acquired DD-Scientific Holdings Limited and its subsidiary DD-Scientific Limited (together, “DD-Scientific”) for approximately $ 53.0 million in cash, net of cash acquired and subject to certain adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The error is demonstrated: the contract names Varex, while the filings identify DD-Scientific, acquired January 14, 2026 for $53.6m and included in Instrumentation. The June 2026 cash, debt and shares are post-DD-Scientific, while the OE anchor is FY2025 and therefore pre-acquisition. That timing can be valid, but the mislabeled contract leaves unresolved whether Varex is a separate transaction. DD-Scientific alone equals only 0.3% of the $17,919m base equity value, but no filed amount permits assessing a separate Varex transaction.
audit_findings.action: Replace the perimeter record with a dated DD-Scientific record and separately establish whether any Varex transaction exists; if it does, obtain its closing status, consideration, financing, dilution and acquired earnings before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may rely on acquisitions whose purchase cost is excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 acquisition spending $821.4m; 2024 acquisition spending $123.7m; 2025 incremental acquisition sales $270.1m; base-versus-bear equity-value difference $4,964m and bull-versus-bear difference $6,999m
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings enter the OE anchor and historical growth, while acquisition consideration remains outside OE; extrapolating that growth without reinvestment inflates forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Investing activities used cash for business acquisitions of $821.4 million and $123.7 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively (see “ Recent Developments ”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, although the amount of growth requiring future acquisitions remains unresolved. Acquisitions supplied $270.1m, or about 61% of the $445.4m increase in 2025 sales, after $821.4m of acquisition spending. Because the valuation assigns $4,964m-$6,999m of equity value to the difference between 0% and 6%-8% growth, unsupported acquisition-dependent growth is reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Decompose 2024-2026 sales and OE growth into organic and acquired contributions, then rerun either with organically supportable growth or with the recurring acquisition investment needed to sustain 6%-8% growth deducted from OE.

audit_findings.title: Revenue growth may require working-capital investment omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 unbilled receivables increased $62.5m while contract liabilities increased $60.1m; 2025 cash-flow changes included $36.6m use for receivables, $42.8m use for inventory and $35.6m source from payables
audit_findings.mechanism: If incremental working capital is omitted, forecast OE recognizes growth-related accounting earnings before the corresponding cash is available to owners.
audit_findings.evidence: The unbilled receivable balance increased from the beginning of the year by $ 62.5 million, or 20.0 %, primarily due to recognizing revenue ahead of achieving billing milestones on certain contracts within the Aerospace and Defense Electronics segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is a valid unresolved possibility, but the cited unbilled-receivable increase was almost offset by the $60.1m increase in contract liabilities. Other working-capital movements were meaningful, yet the supplied record does not isolate normalized organic growth investment from acquisition effects, timing and unrelated balances. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the current reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to receivables, unbilled receivables, inventory, payables and contract liabilities excluding acquisitions and one-time timing effects; derive a normalized working-capital requirement per dollar of organic growth and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Retained interest expense may not reflect refinancing economics
audit_findings.magnitude: $450.0m 2026 notes repaid; $700.0m notes due in 2028 at 2.25%; refinancing-rate effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the valuation uses equity-level OE after interest, refinancing at a higher after-tax coupon would reduce future OE rather than enter through a separate debt deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 28, 2025, we had $2,488.0 million total outstanding indebtedness in senior notes.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves the immediate 2026 question: Teledyne repaid the $450.0m maturity, total debt fell to $2,027.0m, and first-half interest expense declined to $25.9m from $34.9m. The remaining concern is forward-looking: the $700.0m 2028 maturity may be repaid or refinanced, and no filed refinancing terms establish a present adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Monitor the funding plan for the 2028 notes; once repayment or refinancing terms are available, rerun OE using the resulting after-tax interest expense and corresponding cash balance.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain nonrecurring below-the-line gains and tax benefits
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.0m pretax debt-extinguishment gain and $32.5m FY2025 tax benefit; combined after-tax anchor effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained one-time gain or tax benefit increases anchor OE and is then compounded and capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we repurchased and retired $177.0 million of our fixed rate senior notes, recording a $15.0 million non-cash gain on the extinguishment of this debt, with no comparable amount recorded in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring items are demonstrated, but their retention in the $1,060.4m anchor is unresolved because the anchor reconciliation was not supplied. Their filed amounts together equal 4.5% of anchor OE before accounting for the unknown tax interaction on the debt gain, which is sufficiently large to affect the valuation materially when capitalized.
audit_findings.action: Produce the complete FY2025 OE reconciliation, show the treatment of the $15.0m gain and $32.5m tax benefit separately, and rerun every scenario after removing any amounts retained in the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Potential export-control claims may be neither accrued nor bridged
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.0m civil penalty settled and paid in February 2026; remaining exposures unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unaccrued penalties would reduce the equity bridge or OE, while lost or suspended export privileges could reduce forecast OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: An unfavorable outcome could result in substantial fines and penalties or loss or suspension of export privileges or of particular authorizations that could be material to the Company’s financial position, results of operations or cash flows in and following the period in which such outcome becomes estimable or known.
audit_findings.explanation: One identified historical matter was settled for $1.0m, only about 0.006% of the $17,919m base equity value and not material by itself. However, the June 2026 filing continues to disclose other potential U.S. and foreign trade-compliance violations and possible loss or suspension of privileges. Those are existing unresolved matters, but the record supplies no loss range or revenue exposure with which to establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a matter-by-matter schedule of open disclosures, accrued amounts, estimated loss ranges, affected products and jurisdictions; rerun with any probable or probability-weighted cash loss and any supportable impact on OE or growth.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2022 residual D&A $107.3m; $0 direct effect on the current $1,060.4m anchor under the stated anchor cap
audit_findings.mechanism: Reclassifying eligible residual D&A would increase historical OE and potentially its trend, but it cannot increase the current anchor above latest actual under the MIN(trend, latest) rule.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2022 $107.3m (28.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The $107.3m residual is 28.9% of FY2022 filed D&A and could materially increase that historical year's OE if proven eligible. It does not presently change the valuation, however, because the selected $1,060.4m FY2025 anchor is already below the $1,197m trend and the method prohibits anchoring above latest actual. Leaving the residual expensed is conservative and creates no present overstatement.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2022 residual from filed disclosures and update the historical OE series if warranted; rerun only if the classification changes a separately supported growth assumption, because the current anchor remains capped at FY2025 actual OE.
